voice.text: A mouse squeaks far away, under the grass. [pause] The fox hears it! Which part does that job? Tap your guess.
The fox's big <emphasis>ears</emphasis> have a job. [pause] They catch tiny sounds — like a mouse squeak, far away.
The bushy <emphasis>tail</emphasis> has a job. [pause] It balances the fox when she turns fast. And at night, it wraps her up warm.
The sharp <emphasis>teeth</emphasis> have a job. [pause] Eating meat.
The strong <emphasis>legs</emphasis> have a job. [pause] Running fast!

Now look — the crow! [pause] Different parts. A <emphasis>beak</emphasis> to pick up food. <emphasis>Wings</emphasis> to fly. <emphasis>Claws</emphasis> to grab the branch. [pause] Different parts — but the same needs: food, water, and air.
You have parts with jobs too! [pause] Hands that grab. Teeth of different kinds. [pause] And here is the secret: no animal picks its parts. Every animal is born with parts that fit its life.
Listen to the job. [pause] Then tap the part that does it.
All done! Every part matched its job. [pause] Now show what you know.
Not quite. The ears' job is hearing tiny sounds. [pause] Which part fits this job?
Not quite. The tail's job is balance, and keeping warm. [pause] Which part fits this job?
Not quite. The teeth's job is eating meat. [pause] Which part fits this job?
Not quite. The legs' job is running. [pause] Which part fits this job?
Not quite. The beak's job is picking up food. [pause] Which part fits this job?
Not quite. The wings' job is flying. [pause] Which part fits this job?
Not quite. The claws' job is grabbing the branch. [pause] Which part fits this job?
Not quite. Fur is soft hair, like the fox's coat. [pause] Look again — what covers this animal?
Not quite. Feathers belong to birds. [pause] Look again — what covers this animal?
Not quite. Scales are smooth little plates, like on a fish. [pause] Look again — what covers this animal?
Yes! [pause] Big ears catch tiny sounds, far away.
Yes! [pause] The bushy tail wraps around her like a blanket — and balances her when she runs.
Yes! [pause] Sharp teeth are made for eating meat.
Yes! [pause] Strong legs let the fox run and pounce.
Yes! [pause] Claws curl around the branch and hold on tight.
Yes! [pause] The beak is the crow's food-picker. It has no hands!
Yes! [pause] Soft fur covers the rabbit and keeps it warm.
Yes! [pause] Feathers cover the duck. Birds are the feather group.
Yes! [pause] Smooth scales cover the fish.
Yes! [pause] The snake has scales too. No fur, no feathers.
Which part does the hearing job for the fox?
Why does the fox have sharp teeth?
The fox and the crow both need…
What covers a bird's body?
In the fable, the crow held the cheese with its…
<soft>You can match parts to jobs!</soft> [pause] Well done.
Good try! Let's watch the jobs once more.
Lesson done! Now go look up the fox, and find one job a fox part does.
